title: Evasion Attack and Defense on Machine Learning Models in Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey
domain: Evasion attacks and defenses on ML models in cyber-physical systems

analysis_policy.exclude_scope: References, author bios/photos, acknowledgments, appendix, nomenclature
analysis_policy.notes: Span tags retained; mixed HTML/markdown tables kept.

section_flow.objective: Motivate evasion threats to ML in CPS, review related work, clarify scope/terminology, and present structure.
notable_moves: Terminology clarification and survey methodology appear in intro before technical content

evidence_locators.claim: States survey methodology/scope and clarifies terminology after highlighting evasion threats and survey gap.

hook.evidence: Highlights importance of ML in CPS and vulnerability to evasion attacks.

gap.evidence: Notes lack of comprehensive CPS-focused evasion attack/defense surveys.

yes_but.evidence: Acknowledges related works but stresses missing CPS-specific treatment and full taxonomy.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions: attacker taxonomy, CPS evasion attack survey, defense taxonomy, gaps and lessons.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focus on evasion attacks/defenses on ML models in CPS across layers and stages.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate CPS evasion risk; clarify methodology/scope/terminology; provide attacker taxonomy; survey attacks; survey defenses; discuss gaps; summarize lessons and conclude.

taxonomy.classification_strategy: by attacker attributes and attack family
axes: Attacker attributes (knowledge, proximity, strategy, goal, perceptibility, source)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Figures/tables support taxonomy axes and attack/defense summaries; background uses diagrams for CPS layers; defense section may include comparison tables; lessons/gaps text-heavy.

figures.purpose: depict attacker attribute taxonomy and attack families

lesson_blocks.lesson: Multiple attacker attributes expose varied CPS vulnerabilities and guide defenses.
Gradient vs non-gradient categories capture most CPS evasion tactics.
Stage-aligned defenses (data, training, model, detector) map to attack surfaces.
Future work must address adaptive attackers and practical deployment constraints for defenders.

synthesis.aha_moment: Framing CPS evasion by attacker attributes then pairing attack families with stage-aligned defenses makes a large threat space navigable and actionable.

methodology.selection_criteria: stated survey methodology; details of databases/keywords not fully enumerated

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce topic then enumerate taxonomy axes or stage-specific methods; signpost subsections clearly.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Intro with methodology and terminology
steps: Motivate CPS evasion risk and survey gap.
Present survey methodology and scope early.
Clarify key terminology before technical sections.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Establishes clarity and credibility before diving into taxonomy.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Attacker-attribute taxonomy before attack families
steps: Define attacker attributes (knowledge, proximity, strategy, goal, perceptibility, source).
Then survey attack families (gradient vs non-gradient) with examples.
Use figures/tables to keep axes clear.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Attributes frame the threat model, making subsequent attack families easier to map.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Stage-aligned defenses
steps: Group defenses by stage (dataset, training, model, auxiliary detector).
Highlight trade-offs and link each to attack surfaces.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Parallel structure eases mapping from attacks to mitigations.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Gaps split by attacker vs defender
steps: Provide joint challenges and future directions.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Separating perspectives surfaces asymmetric priorities and joint needs.

notes: Counts heuristic; several lists; figures/tables across taxonomy and attacks/defenses. Encoding artifacts may remain in tables.
